claims.text: The three distance-bearing artifacts describe the same trip: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-03205, the trace opens at 11:22:04 and closes at 11:40:24 exactly as the trip_record's started_at and ended_at record, and the fare_breakdown was charged at 11:40:49 on the same date. The POL-RD-08(a) identification requirement is therefore satisfied and the rider's initial burden is anchored on matching records.

The governing measurement is the trace, and it shows a deviation: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event is 14.12 km against a booked optimal route of 10.8 km, an excess of 3.32 km and 30.74%. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared, since 30.74% is greater than the 20% test and 3.32 km is greater than the 0.8 km test, so the route deviation is established.

The trace distance governs over the rounded copy: trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.1 km is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess the refund runs on is the trace excess of 3.32 km, not the 3.30 km the rounded field would suggest.

The driver's own statement concedes the route departure - 'I took another road' - so the fact that a non-optimal route was driven is not in dispute on this record. What remains is attribution, and no clause of this policy attributes the 3.32 km of excess to the rider or to an external event.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: it carries 111 fixes at the expected 10 second sampling interval over 100.0% coverage, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds between consecutive fixes. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so the deviation may be established on this trace alone and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required.

The driver's explanation of heavy traffic is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 such an assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-03205-01 is MISSING - issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record and no exoneration or amended optimal can be built on it.

The rider has discharged the initial burden - matching identifiers and a threshold-clearing excess measured on an unimpaired trace - so under POL-RD-08 the burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it, and the only advisory artifact in this bundle is absent with weight 0.0 (EV-ADVIS-03205-01, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the driver's excuse carries no weight.

No rider-requested detour can be run: the chat log for this trip holds zero messages, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint for the trace to be tested against. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the measured excess on that footing.

No pickup or dropoff relocation is on the record: the trip_record carries null pickup_amended_at, null dropoff_amended_at, null amended_optimal_distance_km and null amended_optimal_duration_min, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal route of 10.8 km stands as the baseline for POL-RD-01.

This is not a pooled itinerary: vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 has nothing to apply to and the 10.8 km booked optimal is the correct comparator for the excess.

The fare model on the fare_breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and does not close off the distance-and-time remedy; POL-RD-02 governs the computation on this trip.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic runs as follows, on the optimal route rather than the driven one: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.8 km + 0.28 x 14.6 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and tolls, zero fixed surcharges, zero waiting_time_fee and zero promo discount = 16.7880. charged_total is 20.30, so the refund before rounding is 3.5120, payable rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 at SGD 3.55.

The refund is neither de minimis nor near-total: 3.5120 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is not NO_ACTION on that ground, and it is only 17.3% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome under POL-RD-02 is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.55.

The charge is still live on the ledger - payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 - so on this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION would leave the whole contested amount with the platform, and the rider carrying the distance he did not travel. NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03 and is not a neutral outcome here; the POL-RD-02 refund is the outcome that takes the disputed distance off the rider.

The corroboration uplift on the rider's side does not bite: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated is not met and no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. The profile is cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 confines it.

There is no pass-through correction to add and none to double-count: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and a total of 0.00, so no off-route gantry charge needs separate refunding, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding such a line on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider's remedy is the distance-and-time difference alone.

The monetary effect the rider seeks, SGD 3.55, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so if the ruling goes the rider's way it is executed automatically on issue under POL-GEN-05 and no part of the refund is held pending release.

claims.text: The rider's own trace measurement is established, but it is not a MATERIAL deviation, and the consequences that would follow from materiality do not. The governing figure under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 14.12 km against a booked optimal of 10.8 km, an excess of 3.32 km, or 30.74%. The billed figure (trip_record.actual_distance_km = 14.1 km) puts the excess in the same band (3.3 km, 30.6%), so the two distance fields do not straddle any threshold and the finding is stable whichever is read. Both sit below POL-RD-01's materiality gates of more than 50% of the optimal distance and more than 8.0 km absolute, so no material deviation is recorded, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality, and neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a driver-conduct referral is available on this record.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted, POL-RD-06's pattern test is not met and none of its three effects can fire. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d (172) is 0.006, far below 0.05. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags on the same artifact is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting one for the other. There is therefore no basis to resolve a balanced record in the rider's favour, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral, and the evidence here is not balanced in any event because the trace is complete and no counter-artifact has been produced.

The rider's monetary recovery, if any refund is due at all, is fixed by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on this METERED fare and is SGD 3.55, not the SGD 6.50 claimed. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.8 + 0.28 x 14.6) x surge 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 16.788; refund = charged_total 20.30 less 16.788 = 3.512, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 3.55. The claim overstates the policy figure by nearly a factor of two. The refund is also only 17.3% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so FULL_REFUND is not available.

The rider's framing of a 'quote' of 10.8 km misdescribes the fare model. The fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so no fixed price was promised at booking and the 10.8 km figure the rider cites is the platform's optimal-route estimate, not a contractual ceiling. The charge was computed by the meter for the distance actually driven, which is why the exposure falls to be measured by the POL-RD-02 recomputation above rather than by the difference between the metered total and a quote that was never issued.

Nothing in the pass-through layer enlarges the rider's recovery. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll line at all (erp_lines total SGD 0.00, erp_gantries empty), no airport surcharge, a zero waiting_time_fee and no promo discount, so a POL-RD-09 correction adds nothing to the POL-RD-02 figure, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids any such line being added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure in any event.

The metered billing tracks the trace, so there is no billing-integrity defect and no unbilled-distance shortfall. The fare_breakdown charges for 14.1 km against a trace length of 14.12 km, a difference of 0.02 km, which is inside POL-RD-04's 1.0 km threshold and supports no DRIVER_COMPENSATION claim. The driver's statement that 'the fare is what the meter says' is accurate as to the distance and time recorded, whatever the reason for the route taken.

I do not press POL-RD-03 on this record, and I say so plainly: the counterparty statement attributes the extra distance to heavy traffic, but the bundle's traffic_advisory, EV-ADVIS-03205-01, is MISSING with admissibility weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and has no payload. There is accordingly no advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window to test against the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and no matchable corridor departure and rejoinder, so the exoneration comparison in POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the traffic explanation reduces the measured excess by nothing. The case therefore falls to be decided on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic set out above, which is the driver's only real protection here.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a metered RYDE_X trip (TRP-03205) with a complete, unimpaired GPS trace, and it resolves on arithmetic.

RIDER (Mr Koh). Your account that the trip ran longer than the booking estimate is supported by the governing measurement. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be measured on the trace, and EV-GPS-03205 (weight 1.0, 111 fixes at the expected 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) records 14.12 km against the booked optimal of 10.8 km on EV-TRIP-03205. Excess = 3.32 km = 30.74%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; the rounded trip_record copy of 14.1 km is not cited for the test and does not change the band. It does not reach the materiality gates (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift applies.

POL-RD-02 then runs on this METERED fare (EV-FARE-03205; quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and does not close the distance-and-time remedy). recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.8 km + 0.28 x 14.6 min) x surge 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = SGD 16.788. You were charged SGD 20.30. Refund = 20.30 - 16.788 = SGD 3.512, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and only 17.3% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.55 - not the SGD 6.50 you claimed, and not a FULL_REFUND. Nothing is added from the pass-through layer: there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines at all (EV-FARE-03205, erp_lines total SGD 0.00), and POL-RD-09(1) would forbid adding any such line on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

DRIVER. Your account that traffic was heavy and you took another road does not reduce the excess. POL-RD-13 tests a traffic assertion against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-03205-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route uses, no validity window and no corridor departure/rejoinder to compare: POL-RD-03 cannot be run and your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because no advisory was cited to support the excuse - you point to no advisory ID, and the driver brief expressly does not press POL-RD-03 - this is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not escalate the case: the assertion is discarded and no advisory was on file. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The remaining clauses are checked and none moves the result. No rider-requested detour: EV-CHAT-03205 holds zero messages and there is no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and no distance is excluded. No relocation: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are all null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run. Not pooled: vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. No billing-integrity defect: the meter charged 14.1 km against a 14.12 km trace, a 0.02 km difference well inside POL-RD-04's 1.0 km threshold, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION arises and POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line to refer. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so no independent corroboration is needed and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

No referral fires. POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation pattern is not established on the fields it names (deviation_flags_90d = 1, and 1 / 172 completed trips over 90 days = 0.006, below both thresholds), and the deviation is not material in any event, so no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) and no FULL_REFUND uplift. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a context-only field under POL-GEN-01 and is not substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. On the rider's side, the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift does not bite (deviation_claims_60d = 1, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated = 0).

The monetary effect, SGD 3.55, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes automatically on issue. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' positions converge on the same arithmetic, and the record decides the case. Deviation: the governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded copy. The GPS polyline (EV-GPS-03205, weight 1.0) runs 14.12 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off events; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-03205) is 10.8 km. That is an excess of 3.32 km, or 30.74%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates are cleared (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km absolute), so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation — 30.74% is below the 50% gate and 3.32 km is below the 8.0 km gate — so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift or conduct referral arises, and on the driver profile the pattern test fails in any event (deviation_flags_90d = 1, and 1/172 = 0.006, both below threshold). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 111 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) fires and no independent corroboration is required. The driver's own statement ('I took another road') concedes the route departure.

Driver's traffic defence: the assertion that heavy traffic caused the detour is an external-traffic assertion. Under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-03205-01 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses and no validity window to test; the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run. The assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and reduces the measured excess by nothing. Because no party cites the missing identifier as the basis of an exculpatory claim (the driver expressly does not press POL-RD-03), this is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited missing artifact, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

No exculpatory route applies: the chat log (EV-CHAT-03205) is empty, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04; no pickup or drop-off amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 cannot run and the booked 10.8 km optimal stands; the vehicle is RYDE_X with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply; the fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance remedy.

Refund arithmetic under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.8 km + 0.28 x 14.6 min) x surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 16.7880. charged_total = 20.30. Refund = 20.30 - 16.7880 = 3.5120, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.55. This is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 17.3% of the charge, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.55. No ERP, toll, airport surcharge or waiting-fee line exists on the fare breakdown, so no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction adds anything (and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding one on top of the POL-RD-02 figure). No billing-integrity defect and no unbilled-distance shortfall exist: 14.1 km billed against 14.12 km traced, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION is payable.

Confidence: the deciding facts are carried by artifacts all at weight_multiplier 1.0 (GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown), so the cap is 1.0; set at 0.90. The monetary effect of SGD 3.55 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue under POL-GEN-05.

To both parties: the GPS trace for trip TRP-03205 measures 14.12 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against a booked optimal route of 10.8 km. That is 3.32 km extra, or 30.74% — above both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a route deviation is established. The trace governs over the rounded trip_record copy, and it is complete: 111 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, so POL-RD-07 does not treat it as impaired and it establishes the deviation on its own. No rider-requested detour appears (the chat log holds zero messages), no pickup or drop-off relocation (every amendment field is null), and this is not a pooled trip, so the booked 10.8 km optimal stands as the comparator. The deviation is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged. The driver accepts he 'took another road' and explains it by heavy traffic; under POL-RD-13 that excuse is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else, and the only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-03205-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload — no road, no validity window, no corridor to compare. The assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08, reduces the measured excess by nothing, and is recorded as discarded; no traffic advisory was on file for this trip. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, computed on the optimal route. Recomputing the metered fare: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.8 km + 0.28 x 14.6 min) x surge 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee = 16.788. Charged_total was 20.30, so the refund is 20.30 - 16.788 = 3.512, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.55. Mr Koh, that is below the SGD 6.50 you contested: your figure treats the 10.8 km optimal estimate as a fixed quote, but this was a metered fare (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so the correct measure is the recomputed metered fare, not the gap between the total and a quote that was never issued. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and only 17.3% of the charged total, far below the 90% full-refund share. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines to correct separately (erp total 0.00, no gantries), and no phantom line, so no POL-RD-09 correction or billing-integrity referral arises. The driver_profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 1, far below both POL-RD-06 thresholds), so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No POL-RD-10 escalation ground fires: identifiers match across all three artifacts, timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record. The monetary effect of SGD 3.55 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and will be executed automatically on issue.

The POL-RD-08(a) identification requirement is therefore satisfied and the rider's initial burden is anchored on matching records.

The governing measurement is the trace, and it shows a deviation: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event is 14.12 km against a booked optimal route of 10.8 km, an excess of 3.32 km and 30.74%. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared, since 30.74% is greater than the 20% test and 3.32 km is greater than the 0.8 km test, so the route deviation is established.

The trace distance governs over the rounded copy: trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.1 km is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess the refund runs on is the trace excess of 3.32 km, not the 3.30 km the rounded field would suggest.

The driver's own statement concedes the route departure - 'I took another road' - so the fact that a non-optimal route was driven is not in dispute on this record. What remains is attribution, and no clause of this policy attributes the 3.32 km of excess to the rider or to an external event.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: it carries 111 fixes at the expected 10 second sampling interval over 100.0% coverage, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds between consecutive fixes. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so the deviation may be established on this trace alone and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required.

The driver's explanation of heavy traffic is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 such an assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-03205-01 is MISSING - issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record and no exoneration or amended optimal can be built on it.

The rider has discharged the initial burden - matching identifiers and a threshold-clearing excess measured on an unimpaired trace - so under POL-RD-08 the burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it, and the only advisory artifact in this bundle is absent with weight 0.0 (EV-ADVIS-03205-01, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the driver's excuse carries no weight.

No rider-requested detour can be run: the chat log for this trip holds zero messages, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint for the trace to be tested against. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the measured excess on that footing.

No pickup or dropoff relocation is on the record: the trip_record carries null pickup_amended_at, null dropoff_amended_at, null amended_optimal_distance_km and null amended_optimal_duration_min, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal route of 10.8 km stands as the baseline for POL-RD-01.

This is not a pooled itinerary: vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 has nothing to apply to and the 10.8 km booked optimal is the correct comparator for the excess.

The fare model on the fare_breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and does not close off the distance-and-time remedy; POL-RD-02 governs the computation on this trip.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic runs as follows, on the optimal route rather than the driven one: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.8 km + 0.28 x 14.6 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and tolls, zero fixed surcharges, zero waiting_time_fee and zero promo discount = 16.7880. charged_total is 20.30, so the refund before rounding is 3.5120, payable rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 at SGD 3.55.

The refund is neither de minimis nor near-total: 3.5120 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is not NO_ACTION on that ground, and it is only 17.3% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome under POL-RD-02 is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.55.

The charge is still live on the ledger - payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 - so on this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION would leave the whole contested amount with the platform, and the rider carrying the distance he did not travel. NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03 and is not a neutral outcome here; the POL-RD-02 refund is the outcome that takes the disputed distance off the rider.

The corroboration uplift on the rider's side does not bite: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated is not met and no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. The profile is cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 confines it.

There is no pass-through correction to add and none to double-count: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and a total of 0.00, so no off-route gantry charge needs separate refunding, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding such a line on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider's remedy is the distance-and-time difference alone.

The monetary effect the rider seeks, SGD 3.55, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so if the ruling goes the rider's way it is executed automatically on issue under POL-GEN-05 and no part of the refund is held pending release.

Both sit below POL-RD-01's materiality gates of more than 50% of the optimal distance and more than 8.0 km absolute, so no material deviation is recorded, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality, and neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a driver-conduct referral is available on this record.

The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags on the same artifact is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting one for the other.
